title: Protocol to culture and image pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumor slices to study T cell migration
protocol: Isolate CD8+ T cells from mouse spleen using EasySep Mouse CD8 T Cell Isolation Kit following manufacturer’s recommendation with slight modifications.
Activate and expand isolated CD8+ T cells using Dynabeads Mouse T-Activator CD3/CD28, following manufacturer’s recommendation with slight modifications.
Seed 100K cells per well in a 96 well round bottom plate in 100 μL of media with 2.5 μL of activation beads.
Culture the seeded cells in Immunocult media supplemented with 30 U/mL of IL-2 to encourage proliferation.
Activate cells for at least 4 days prior to removal of the CD3/CD28 beads.
Add 50–100 μL of fresh immunocult media with 30 U/mL of IL-2 during activation without disturbing cell pellet.
Split cells into 3 new wells and replenish with fresh media up to 100 μL if culture media is turning yellow or cells are expanding rapidly.
Remove CD3/CD28 activation beads after 4 days: gently mix the cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 300g for 10 min.
Resuspend cell pellet in 2 mL of fresh Immunocult media in round bottom tubes.
Mix thoroughly and place the tube containing the cell suspension in the magnetic separator following the EasySep protocol.
If the cell pellet is large, resuspend the cell pellet in 4 mL (splitting suspension in two) and perform magnetic separation on both suspensions individually.
Populations can be mixed after negative selection.
Verify isolation purity of CD8+ T cells using an anti-CD8 antibody and flow cytometry.
Assess purity via flow cytometry before use in subsequent experiments.
Optionally, stain additional markers such as CD45 or CD3 for more detailed characterization.
Culture primary activated CD8+ T cells immediately after isolation or keep them in culture up to 7–8 days post-isolation.
Prepare freezing medium (15% DMSO in FBS) and freeze down cells if immediate use is not required.
Thaw frozen T cells in a water bath at 37°C for 1-2 minutes.
Wash thawed cells in 10 mL of warm Immunocult media.
Spin down the cell suspension at 300g for 10 minutes.
Seed thawed cells into a 96 well plate at a density of 2 × 10^2 cells per well in 100 μL of Immunocult media supplemented with 200 U/mL IL-2.
Let cells recover for 24–48 hours before starting subsequent experiments.
Split each well into three new wells and add fresh Immunocult media with 200 U/mL IL-2 to 150 μL if media changes color or cell pellet doubles in size post-thaw.
Prepare a 1.5% agarose solution in TAE buffer.
Microwave the agarose solution until completely dissolved.
Pour the agarose solution into a cell culture dish.
Place the dish on ice until the gel hardens.
Filter sterilize a solution of 100 mM HEPES in 2× PBS.
Mix rat tail collagen type I at a ratio of 1:1 with sterile 100 mM HEPES and complete volume with sterile 1× PBS buffer to prepare a 3 mg/mL solution.
Coat 6-well inserts with 250 μL of the collagen solution.
Coat 24-well inserts with 50 μL of the collagen solution.
Allow the coated inserts to dry in a sterile laminar flow hood for 1–2 hours.
Store unused inserts at 4°C for up to two weeks.
Harvest PDA tumor from KPC or KPCT mice.
Transfer the harvested tumor to a conical tube containing sterile ice-cold PBS with 10 μg/mL STI and 1× P/S.
Cut a small block from the agarose gel, slightly larger than the tumor.
Adhere the agarose to the specimen disk of the vibratome stage using Loctite superglue.
Glue the tumor directly in front of the agarose block.
Fill the tray with ice-cold sterile PBS once the glue dries.
Section the tumor at a 300–350 μm thickness with the vibratome speed set on a 3 mm/s and the vibration frequency set on 8 mm.
Optimize slice thickness, speed and vibration frequency based on the machine and tissue type.
Transfer each slice carefully with fine forceps to a conical tube or culture plate containing fresh sterile ice-cold PBS with 10 μg/mL STI and 1× P/S for transport.
Discard the first couple of slices and adhered bottom portion of the tumor.
Prepare culture inserts by adding 1.1 mL or 400 μL of warm RPMI 1640 with L-glutamine supplemented with 10% FBS, 14.5 mM Hepes, 1× P/S, 5 μg/mL Plasmocin and 10 μg/mL STI.
Transfer slices to prepared organotypic culture inserts.
Ensure slices lay flat and do not overlap in the culture insert for optimal nutrient and gas exchange.
Immobilize pancreatic adenocarcinoma tumor slides on a tissue culture dish using slice anchors for handling and imaging.

Overlay explanted tissue with 100 μL or 50 μL of RPMI 1640 with L-glutamine supplemented with 10% FBS, 14.5 mM Hepes, 1× P/S, 5 μg/mL Plasmocin and 10 μg/mL STI on the 6-well and 24-well inserts, respectively.
Culture slices at 37°C in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator and either use immediately or within 4 days to ensure viability and integrity.
Replace media both above and below insert daily.
Cut a square piece of parafilm larger than a 35 mm dish.
Cut a smaller circular hole in the middle of the parafilm, smaller than the diameter of the objective.
Attach paper tape on all four corners of the parafilm.
Place the parafilm like a collar on the objective with the lens through the smaller hole.
Wrap the objective tightly with bubble wrap above the parafilm to act as insulation.
Place an O-ring around the 35-mm dish containing prewarmed sterile PBS.
Place the 35-mm dish onto the heating element on the microscope stage.
Lower the objective to the water in the dish.
Make a seal with the parafilm around the 35-mm dish.
Attach the parafilm to the stage.
Let the system equilibrate for at least 2 hours before imaging.
Find positions of interest within the tumor slice by visualizing CD8+ T cells and KPC tumor tissue.
Visualize tdTomato+ carcinoma cells in KPCT tumor slices using multiphoton fluorescence.
Visualize collagen by SHG at 880-nm two-photon excitation.
Take images of T cell migration in 3-D at 1.5 min intervals.
Acquire images at a total imaging duration of at least 45 min, up to 2–3 h.
Acquire images at a step size of 5 μm within a 75 μm deep z section.
Perform quantitative analysis of T cell migration for post-processing and cell tracking.
Stain KPC tumor slices with 5 μM CellTracker Red CMTPX for 15–20 minutes.
Rinse tissue in RPMI 1640 supplemented with components as specified.
Collect and count cultured T cells, harvesting at least 2.0 × 10^5 viable cells.
Centrifuge collected T cells and resuspend in L-15 media with 1% FBS.
Add 2 μM stock CellTracker Green CMFDA to the cell suspension at a 1:1 ratio.
Incubate cell suspension in a water bath at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Wash cell suspension twice with L-15 media supplemented with 10% FBS by spinning down at 300g for 5 minutes.
Transfer individual tumor slices to 24-well organotypic culture inserts.
Resuspend stained T cells in a total volume of 100 μL of L-15 media with specified supplements.
Overlay resuspended T cells onto the tumor slice.
Incubate at 37°C in a 0% CO2 humidified incubator for 1 hour.
Rinse the tumor slice gently by dipping it into warm media to remove T cells that did not adhere.
Transfer the rinsed tissue to a 35-mm tissue culture plate.
Place the side with overlaid T cells upward on the tissue culture plate.
Handle the slices minimally and only at the edges to minimize tissue damage.
Gently place a slice anchor (tissue harp) on top of the tissue to hold it in place.
Overlay the tissue with 5 mL of L-15 media supplemented with 10% FBS, 1× P/S, 5 μg/mL Plasmocin, and 10 μg/mL STI.
Place the prepared slice on the two-photon microscope stage.
Proceed with time-lapse imaging.
